beats.narration_text: Bula. This is Liam, in for Bear. audit_review_queue.py is a read-only batch inspector for Brutalist reels. Give it a numbered list of reel paths and it walks every folder: hashing beat sheets, probing master MP4s, sampling per-beat source clips at the 70-percent mark for contact sheets, and flagging anything worth a human look — stale masters, pantry paths that should be code, math layout mismatches. It never approves. It never publishes. It writes evidence and stops.

beats.narration_text: Before the script reads a single file, fix the first misconception. audit_review_queue.py does not decide if a reel ships. The script's own docstring says it plainly: never approves, never publishes. It reads source structure, samples frames, and writes review leads — flags that point a human where to look, not proof of fabrication. This is Liam. Let's take it apart.

beats.narration_text: Three required flags, all mandatory. --list points at a text file of numbered reel entries. --root is the books directory the script resolves relative paths against. --out is where the evidence lands: numbered source JSON files, contact sheets, and a rolled-up audit.json. The batch file format is human-readable: a number, a dot, a description label, then the path. The parser extracts the last slash-containing token from each line.

props.title: audit_review_queue.py — invocation
props.code:
# Three required flags
python3 runtime/scripts/audit_review_queue.py \
  --list  batch.txt   \  # numbered reel list
  --root  /books      \  # resolves relative paths
  --out   /audit-out     # evidence directory

# batch.txt format: number · label · path
  1. The nopunt Skill   youtube/brutalist/claude-liam-brutalist-skill-nopunt
  2. Art help command   youtube/brutalist/claude-liam-brutalist-command-art-help

# Parser: extracts last slash-containing token per line
# Duplicates → ValueError before any reel is opened

beats.narration_text: Per reel, four phases. Parse the list with a strict regex — empty or duplicate entries throw before any reel is touched. Audit opens the beat sheet, probes the master MP4 if one exists, and runs the math layout check. Sample takes source-beat clips — the individual per-beat MP4s — and grabs one frame at 70 percent of each clip's duration. Report writes a numbered JSON per reel plus a rolled-up audit.json with the batch scope and limitations clause.

beats.narration_text: Four finding categories. Math layout errors come from the math_layout_check import — it flags flat notation in FormACard props where structured rendering is required. Pantry paths split two ways: if the visual intent suggests terminal output or notebook rows, it's a replace-with-code lead; otherwise it's a source-artifact-review. Overflow-to-infinity patterns in narration text get their own flag. Every finding carries a confidence field: source-confirmed, routing-review, or review.

props.title: audit_review_queue.py — findings
props.code:
# Four finding categories (all are review leads, not verdicts)

# 1. Math layout — from math_layout_check import
for error in math_layout_errors(sheet):
    findings.append({'category': 'math-layout',
                     'confidence': 'source-confirmed', 'detail': error})

# 2a. Pantry — reproducible (terminal/pytest/notebook)
category = 'replace-with-code-data-or-diagram'

# 2b. Pantry — non-reproducible
category = 'source-artifact-or-illustration-review'

# 3. Overflow-to-infinity narration claim
if re.search(r'overflows? to infinity', narration, re.I):
    findings.append({'category': 'overflow-claim-review',
                     'confidence': 'review'})

beats.narration_text: One design decision worth the Teardown lens: stale master detection. The script compares the master MP4's modification time against the beat sheet's. If the beat sheet is newer than the master, the contact sheet frames you're reviewing may not match what the current sheet describes — the render is stale. The flag is informational. It does not block the audit and does not touch either file. It just names the gap.

props.title: audit_review_queue.py — stale master
props.code:
# Stale master: beat sheet newer than the rendered master MP4
# Written to per-reel JSON; does NOT block the audit

'stale': (
    master.stat().st_mtime < sheet_path.stat().st_mtime
    if master else None
),

# stale = True  → master rendered before the last sheet edit
# stale = False → master is current
# stale = None  → no master MP4 found at all

# The flag names the gap; it never raises and never modifies files.

beats.narration_text: Three hard dependencies at import time. PIL — the script calls Image.new and ImageDraw.Draw to build contact sheets; no Pillow, no contact sheets, no run. math_layout_check — a local module in runtime/scripts; if it's missing, the import fails before argument parsing. ffmpeg and ffprobe — called via subprocess for probing and frame extraction; absent binaries produce empty contact tiles and zero-byte probes with no warning unless ffmpeg is absent from PATH.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real output from a live audit run against the nopunt skill episode — a completed reel with all twelve source clips present. Twelve beats found. Twelve frame samples taken at the 70-percent mark of each per-beat clip. Zero review leads. No pantry paths, no math layout errors, no overflow claims in narration. The output line is the contract: beat count, lead count, sample count — nothing else is printed to stdout.

beats.narration_text: Three failure modes. The first two are hard stops before any reel is touched: an empty list and a list with duplicate paths both raise ValueError immediately. The third is silent: if ffmpeg cannot extract a frame — wrong path format, corrupt clip, codec gap — the contact sheet tile stays blank and the sample record carries status error. The audit continues for all other beats. You find out by looking at the contact sheet image, not by reading stderr.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. The stale-master check is the one signal the rest of the pipeline cannot give you — it names when source and render are out of sync. The 70-percent frame position is a deliberate design choice: it skips the slate frame at clip start and freeze artifacts near the end, capturing a settled mid-play state. What it bites on: silent ffmpeg tile failures look identical to healthy tiles unless you count them. And math_layout_check has no fallback — a missing local module crashes the entire batch before the first reel opens.

artifactLines: Stale-master detection is unique to this tool — it names when render and source are out of sync, which no other pipeline check surfaces.
70%-position sampling is a deliberate design choice: it skips slate frames at clip start and freeze artifacts near the tail, capturing a settled mid-play state.
Silent bites: blank contact tiles look identical to healthy ones (count them); math_layout_check has no fallback and crashes the whole batch if the local module is missing.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Pick two reels you have already delivered — completed episodes with beat_sheet.json present. Write a two-entry batch file: number, a description label, and the reel's relative path from your books root. Run the script with all three flags. Open the audit.json it writes. For each reel, check whether stale is true or null, how many findings landed, and whether all sample statuses are sampled rather than error. If stale is true, your master predates your current sheet. If a sample status is error, find that per-beat clip and check its path.
